actual_scope: Exhaustive centralizer census and normalizer splitting of one 216-dimensional c=1 summand of the historical doubled centre block. The trivial-character (+1,+1) summand is reducible under A_1, with rational invariant subspaces of dimensions 8, 80 and 128.
scope_change_reason: The catalogue card asks for a formal caller or certificate binding. Discussion comment 19144258, continued by the open question in PR #6944, asks whether one 216-dimensional joint eigenspace of the c=1 sign character is irreducible under A_1. This package answers that algebraic question for the trivial-character (+1,+1) summand. It does not add a Lean binding, a characteristic polynomial, or a kappa change.
bottleneck_link: Scoped side result on the historical centre Gram. The selected conditional kappa remains 781451/250000000. A finer invariant subspace does not replace the degree-881 one-slot annihilator and does not admit a supplier.
stop_rule: Stop once the signed-permutation centralizer of the two known involutions is enumerated and either a finer A_1-invariant subspace of one 216-dimensional summand is certified or the further-permutation test is recorded as inconclusive. Do not compute a characteristic polynomial and do not treat a missing involution as irreducibility.
evidence: verify.py enumerates the line-preserving signed permutations, the c=1 centralizer and normalizer, and the dihedral character inner products. Marker PASS_CENTRE_216_NORMALIZER_SPLIT. Centralizer order 16, every joint trace ±216. Normalizer image is dihedral of order 12 with rational isotypic dimensions 8, 80 and 128 on the trivial-character (+1,+1) summand.
author: unpaidmoon
ai_assistance: Prepared by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok assistance. The assistant enumerated the symmetry group and wrote the verifier. This is not an independent human or proof-kernel review.

open_questions.question: Is the 8-dimensional isotypic summand irreducible under A_1?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the smallest rational A_1-invariant subspace this signed-permutation normalizer isolates inside the 216-dimensional summand.
open_questions.first_step: Build a basis of the image of the integer projector sum psi(g) rho(g) and decide whether the restricted block of B_1 has a proper invariant subspace. A missing extra involution is not a proof.
open_questions.blocked_by: The character inner product certifies the dimension without listing a basis. The fork branch cursor/a1-joint-216-charpoly-0702 records the characteristic polynomial of the parent 216-space and was not used to identify this summand.

open_questions.question: Does any signed permutation in the c=1 stabilizer, outside the normalizer of {g,t}, preserve the 8-dimensional summand and act non-scalarly on it?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The centralizer census rules out elements that commute with both g and t. It does not by itself survey elements that fail to normalize the pair.
open_questions.first_step: Test one stabilizer element outside the normalizer against the multiplicity-8 character projector.
open_questions.blocked_by: Preservation of that summand is not implied by the trace of the element on the ambient 4096-dimensional block.

overlap.limits: Closed PRs were searched through local READMEs, TASK metadata and the ledger. No code diffs. The phrase 216-dimensional matches PR #6944, which leaves this irreducibility question open, and does not match another open PR.
